cells.tense: The new thing is at the door and you are already turning it over.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Whatever has shown up unnamed this week, ask it one real question — what is this, actually — then finish the inquiry and move once on what you land on.
cells.core:
Something has arrived that you don't have a name for yet, and your first move is a question rather than a verdict. You turn it over, look from another side, let it stay unfamiliar in your hands. That's not indecision. People notice their own thinking moving when they stand near you.

The curiosity is doing its work. What it hasn't done yet is spend the finding. Hold the thing long enough to land on one answer, then move on that answer the same day, without laying out the reasons. You don't have to know everything about what's arriving. One true answer, acted on, is enough to show you the floor under it.
cells.sheetLine: Ask what's at the door before you name it.
cells.verb: meeting what's newly arriving with fresh, careful attention
cells.place: the threshold where what was outside is crossing in

cells.tense: The next thing is not here yet and you are already interrogating it.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something small and new purely because it interests you, and keep it unjudged. No verdict on where it leads, no explaining it to anyone. Let it be underway and see.
cells.core:
Where something is trying to enter, you've got your ear against the door before it's even knocked. Questions become wanted answers, and wanted answers ask you to know before you find out. What came in as curiosity is being kept small so nothing catches you out. Whatever arrives, you have a read on it first. That reads as being ahead. It also means you're standing where nothing can enter beside you.

You know the other face of this. Not knowing is comfortable when you allow it, and perception lands without argument. This week, give what's next some slack. Do something new without a plan, because it does spark. Hear the thing out before you finish its sentence for it.
cells.sheetLine: You'd rather know early than find out.

cells.tense: The new thing came through the door and you are still standing on the far side.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Sit with a thing that hasn't happened yet — a trip, a talk, whatever's coming — and sense it without fixing it. No plan, no clock, nothing to solve.
cells.core:
The threshold is behind you and the room ahead is quiet. What's arriving arrives without your questions meeting it; it goes into the pile of things to get through. The listening may still be there, but the fresh part of it has thinned, and you answer from the shelf of what's settled. There's no fault in it. The edge of the room has simply gone still.

Nothing has to be pushed back into life by force here. Stay with something that hasn't arrived yet and permit it to remain unformed. No interpretation, no plan, no better question. You don't have to want to know. Seeing what's coming without demanding it is the same muscle in a quieter register. Do that once, and note what it left behind.

cells.tense: You are weighing who pays for what while the door opens without your noticing.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Weigh, openly and honestly, what one choice this week asks of the others in it. Who pays, who gains, is the trade even. Let that reading settle it, and take no further step.
cells.core:
What you offer around a new thing is quietly your own judgment — you sense who a decision costs what, and you've been moving through it without filing the judgment under your name. Call it circumstance, call it the situation. The reading is yours either way, and the others have been leaning on it without saying so.

Your standard is steady and doesn't need calculating to be sound. Take one decision that's sitting with you and put the ledger on the table on purpose. Who pays, who gets something, is the trade even. You don't have to announce the verdict. You only have to read what you already see, and let yourself be the one who saw it.

attempts.check: The weakest claim is the Too Little mechanism: I render it as this person having stopped asking fresh questions under incoming material, and the record only says the seat is running on empty. A reader could reasonably hear that as 'you've gone incurious on purpose' rather than 'you're worn down,' so the cell locates the effect and leaves the cause alone. The asks (a question held a day, a spark started, a sensing toward what hasn't happened, weighing what a choice costs someone) survive a wrong read because each one returns something to the person that costs almost nothing — they teach a little either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying they have shut down; cut it.
